trigger: An airframer launches fps or NGSA and asks for a CFM engine, with no rival narrowbody engine launched or signalled
response: Compete without assuming incumbency; offer the derivative before a clean sheet; pursue a new platform with Safran only if additive
war_game_translation: Do Nothing on engines: the airframe flies the LEAP derivative (cfm_leap_plus). Snapshot: NGSA 2029 gives CFM +14.46 (ducted standard -8.90); fps 2029 gives +1.28 (ducted -16.25). Disclose that CFM commits a new engine against a committed airframe. Safran gate: consent assumed (joint practice)

trigger: An airframer is about to launch fps or NGSA while a rival narrowbody engine (gtf_next, uf_nb Solo or Joint Venture) is launched or credibly signalled
response: Fight campaign by campaign on durability; take early-life risk priced to win; no price war for share's sake
lag: same turn if signalled; otherwise the next turn, before that airframer launches
war_game_translation: launch ducted with aggressive terms, launch year at or before the airframer's (7 development years). Standard terms never beat a launched rival in the snapshot. Snapshot value of defending against losing: NGSA -14.87 against -28.30; fps -20.55 against -29.04. Run whatif with the rival's launch included; options assumes rivals do nothing

trigger: An airframer commits (disclosed, or predicted at about 0.7 or more) to an fps or NGSA launch in 2036-2037 on the RISE open fan
response: Turn the technology into a product when the airframer and airlines are ready; hold the 20% fuel-burn bar
war_game_translation: open_fan launched in 2036 (9 years; ready 2045), standard terms, plus lobby_emissions. Gates G1-G5 in profile section 6. Declare the RISE premium against the LEAP derivative (snapshot 8.63-13.14) within the one-off RISE allowance of $15B. NGSA 2037 on RISE with lobbying: Airbus +17.97 against +16.59 on the LEAP derivative

trigger: An airframer asks for RISE on an airframe launched before 2036
response: Leave the entry date to the airframer; never press it into a wait; GE's own window was the mid-2030s
war_game_translation: No early open_fan launch; disclose that RISE enters service in 2045. Snapshot: NGSA 2029 on RISE leaves Airbus +1.79 against +38.09 on the LEAP derivative, and an early CFM launch only adds capex (fps 2037 on RISE: CFM -15.31 if launched 2026, -9.47 if 2036)

trigger: Rolls-Royce launches an UltraFan narrowbody, Solo
response: No public reaction and no price cut; RISE stays funded; the technical counter is physics (ducted engines get less than half the open fan's gain)
lag: next turn, before the next open airframe launches
war_game_translation: ducted with aggressive terms. Snapshot fps 2029: Boeing +15.33 on UltraFan standard against +16.50 on CFM aggressive; Rolls-Royce aggressive (+17.57) still wins, in which case hold and declare the loss

trigger: Rolls-Royce and Pratt & Whitney launch the UltraFan narrowbody as a Joint Venture
response: As for a Solo launch; GE leaders rejected three-supplier airframes and a geared product for a new narrowbody
war_game_translation: ducted with aggressive terms. Snapshot NGSA 2029: Joint Venture UltraFan +46.35 for Airbus against +48.40 on CFM aggressive; the Joint Venture is worth +10.86 to Pratt & Whitney and +8.87 to Rolls-Royce if Airbus picks it, so treat it as a live threat

trigger: Pratt & Whitney launches a next-generation GTF
response: Durability as the weapon; score by win rate; welcome GTF operators; do not name the rival
war_game_translation: ducted with aggressive terms. Snapshot: NGSA 2029 GTF2 +44.35 for Airbus against +48.40 on CFM aggressive (Pratt & Whitney aggressive, +48.75, still wins); fps 2029 GTF2 +14.39 against +16.50

trigger: Pratt & Whitney orders its GTF durability upgrade (gtf_upgrade)
response: Answer with dated, delivered durability fixes; defend A320neo share on time on wing
war_game_translation: leap_upgrade, alone in its turn. Snapshot: gtf_upgrade alone costs CFM -3.53 and drops nb_dominance to 73% (missed); with leap_upgrade in the same round CFM is +1.41 and nb_dominance 76% (met)

trigger: Rolls-Royce orders its Trent 1000 upgrade (t1000_upgrade)
response: Defend the 787 on fuel burn and time on wing, not price
war_game_translation: genx_upgrade in round 2 (GE alone, no Safran gate). Snapshot: the Trent 1000 upgrade costs CFM -0.98; genx_upgrade adds +0.43 in round 2 (+0.66 in round 1) either way

trigger: Boeing launches a 787 Re-engine
response: Offer the GEnx derivative; the 787 was won on product
war_game_translation: No lever needed: ge_genx_next is the default and needs no commitment. Snapshot: CFM/GE +2.25 (2027 launch) or +1.50 (2031); keep genx_upgrade (+0.16 to +0.28 even on a re-engined 787). On a rival engine the Re-engine costs -5.92 (UltraFan) or -5.43 (Pratt & Whitney)

trigger: Airbus launches an A350 Re-engine
response: Want all the critical platforms; keep talks private; only on additive economics
war_game_translation: No lever. If Rolls-Royce has not launched uf_wb, the Re-engine falls back to GEnx-next (snapshot +4.98 to CFM/GE). Say nothing that presses Airbus

trigger: A rival launches a new widebody engine (uf_wb, pw_wb)
response: No comment on competition; compete on product
war_game_translation: genx_upgrade if not done; nothing else

trigger: An airframer demands aggressive terms or concessions
response: Every order accretive on price, terms and scope; no unmodelled risk; no launch-era pricing; early-life risk only when priced
war_game_translation: standard terms unless a launched rival would otherwise win the airframe. Aggressive terms (+1.4pp airframer margin, value_mult 0.88; provisional) reach every airframe on that engine: snapshot NGSA and fps both on aggressive ducted leaves CFM -25.54. Safran gate: pricing is joint

trigger: Engine maturity slip (engine_maturity_slip) or a durability problem on our engines
response: Admit the gap with numbers; root cause and corrective action; retrofit at natural shop visits; no date without turn-on/turn-off testing
war_game_translation: No new launch to fix it; leap_upgrade if not done. Snapshot: CFM's PV unchanged; airframes lose (NGSA 2029 ducted: Airbus 42.77 to 34.73); open-fan values are unaffected

trigger: A rival durability crisis (gtf_durability_crisis, rr_durability_crisis)
response: No gloating and no public claim on switching customers; expect no near-term share gain while supply binds
war_game_translation: Nothing new; leap_upgrade if not done; disclose durability facts only

trigger: A rival engine test setback (gtf_next_test_setback, ultrafan_test_setback)
response: Let durability speak; compete campaign by campaign
war_game_translation: Keep or launch ducted only if an unlaunched airframe could still move to it; otherwise no move (inference)

trigger: Supply-chain crunch (supply_chain_crunch)
response: Own the problem; engineers and kaizens in supplier plants; buffer inventory; no public blame of suppliers or Safran
war_game_translation: Strain rises 1.5x: never stack two commitments in a turn (snapshot: leap_upgrade plus genx_upgrade in round 1 falls from +4.18 to +3.48); no new launch unless defensive

trigger: Fuel-price spike (fuel_price_spike)
response: Sustainability and fuel burn as the next basis of competition; the fleet already runs on approved sustainable aviation fuel
war_game_translation: No lever change: the spike adds 1.5pp to every new airframe whatever the engine. Use it in RISE disclosures (view)

trigger: FAA certification scrutiny on Boeing or a Boeing quality escape
response: Support Boeing publicly; no date ahead of Boeing or the FAA; pace shipments to its real rate; payment terms rather than halted deliveries
war_game_translation: No order change. For a 2037 RISE fps, FAA scrutiny plus Delay Tactics push entry to 2046 and miss the open_fan metric; a 2036 airframe launch absorbs both

trigger: Narrowbody demand shock (nb_demand_shock)
response: Cut cost and capex fast, keep enough capacity for the recovery, protect next-generation technology
war_game_translation: No launch, no RISE cancellation. Snapshot: CFM's delta PV unchanged

trigger: The replacement wave from 2037 (demand weights rising to a 2044-2046 peak)
response: Plan on the base case and treat tailwinds as upside; RISE was meant for the mid-2030s
war_game_translation: The round-3 RISE window: a 2036-2037 airframe enters service into the peak. Earlier launches on CFM engines pay CFM more: an NGSA on the LEAP derivative is worth +18.89 launched in 2026 and +6.60 in 2037 (snapshot)

trigger: An airframer launches on cfm_ducted before CFM has committed the engine
response: Follow the airframer's real programme; do not spend ahead of a launch
war_game_translation: The airframe is already on the LEAP derivative; do not launch ducted afterwards (snapshot: a 2031 ducted after an NGSA 2029 on the LEAP derivative only adds -5.55 of capex)

trigger: A launched CFM engine has no airframe (the threat passed or the airframe went elsewhere)
response: Cut engineering when no airframe is in sight, but protect the underlying technology
war_game_translation: cancel it, if no live airframe flies it. Snapshot: a 2027 ducted with no airframe is -7.55 kept, -4.80 if cancelled in round 2. Never cancel open_fan while an airframer may still launch on it

trigger: Boeing launches fps as a Joint Venture with Embraer, or Embraer seeks an engine partner
response: No evidence of a GE stance on Embraer
war_game_translation: The fps Joint Venture leaves the engine choice to Boeing. embraer_partner stays off: snapshot PV is negative in every round (-0.10, -0.14, -0.16) (inference)
